items.name: Code review
items.description: Reviews a change for real problems before a commit: reads the diff and the code around it, traces one input to the failure before believing a finding, ranks what holds by severity, and never fixes while reviewing. Ships the reviewer prompt for a clean-context subagent.

items.name: Commit
items.description: Commits the change in the working tree with a message in the repository's own style: only what is staged or named, one concern per commit, hooks never skipped.

items.name: PR description
items.description: Writes a pull request's title and description from the branch's commits and diff: what changes and why, how it was really checked, what to review closely.

items.name: Debug a failing test
items.description: Reproduces a failing or flaky test alone, reads the whole failure, narrows it down and fixes the cause — never by weakening the test.

items.name: Mutation check
items.description: Checks that tests would catch a bug: breaks the changed code one edit at a time, runs the tests, and writes a test for every break that still passes.

items.name: Ponytail Kibo
items.description: The laziest solution that works: YAGNI, reuse before new code, stdlib before custom code, one line before fifty. A senior dev's reflex for any coding task, in three intensity levels — lite, full, ultra.

items.name: Allure TestOps
items.description: Hands the model the Allure TestOps domain as the tools see it: which id comes from which reference tool, the read-then-write map of the 30 tools, ready-made chains (find a case, read its steps, its history, run a selection, read the results), the JSON shapes of tags, members and custom fields, paging and sort, what the server deliberately cannot do, and how to read each kind of error answer. Ships aql.md beside SKILL.md: the query language as the stand accepts it - every field of test cases, results and launches, the operators, epoch dates, subfields and the ready-made queries. Use together with the testops MCP entry, which this skill describes.

items.name: /changelog
items.description: Adds a CHANGELOG.md line under Unreleased for the change in the working tree.

items.name: /commit
items.description: Commits the working tree's change with a message matching the repository's log and commit rules.

items.name: /release-notes
items.description: Drafts release notes since the last tag from CHANGELOG.md, merged PRs and the log: Added, Changed, Fixed, Removed.

items.name: TLS certificate rejected
items.description: Kubernetes role: x509 errors, an expired or missing ingress certificate, cert-manager not Ready.

items.name: Job or CronJob fails
items.description: Kubernetes role: BackoffLimitExceeded, DeadlineExceeded, pods gone after the TTL, a CronJob suspended, skipped behind a hanging run or past its missed starts.

items.name: GitHub
items.description: GitHub's remote MCP server: issues, pull requests, code search. Needs a personal access token.

items.name: Context7
items.description: Up-to-date documentation and code examples for libraries and frameworks. Remote server, works without a key.

items.name: Grafana
items.description: Dashboards, Prometheus, Loki and Tempo queries, alerts and incidents of your Grafana, read-only. Runs with uvx; needs the Grafana URL and a service account token.

items.name: Browser
items.description: A real Chromium the agent drives: opens a page, reads it as an accessibility tree with refs, then clicks, fills and extracts through them. Runs the `agent-browser mcp` command of the open-source agent-browser CLI (Apache-2.0, vercel-labs); install it once with `npm i -g agent-browser && agent-browser install`, which downloads Chrome for Testing.

items.name: Core Components
items.description: @alfalab/core-components as the model needs it while writing UI: 4 tools that list the components, return one component's props with types and defaults, its demo code, and its changelog — one version, or everything between two. Runs the published package @alfalab/core-components-mcp with npx; it takes no token, reads no environment and makes no network calls, the component data ships inside it. Needs Node 24+. The same package installs the matching skill for a project: npx @alfalab/core-components-mcp@latest add-skill writes .agents/skills/core-components/. The package declares neither a license nor a repository field, so treat it as Alfa-Bank's own unpublished-source tool.

items.name: Confluence
items.description: Confluence Server / Data Center for an agent, 6 tools only: read a page by id, CQL search, create and update content, upload and download an attachment. Runs the MIT package @atlassian-dc-mcp/confluence (github.com/b1ff/atlassian-dc-mcp) with npx and talks to CONFLUENCE_HOST alone; the token it asks for is the one Confluence hands out at Profile > Personal Access Tokens. A page body comes back as Confluence storage XML unless the call asks for bodyMode text with maxBodyChars — that mode is readable but drops link URLs, attachment filenames and macro parameter names, while updateContent and its oldStr/newStr edits must stay in storage XML. Under a context path set CONFLUENCE_API_BASE_PATH=/wiki (or the full URL); a plain http instance needs the scheme spelled out in CONFLUENCE_HOST. NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=1 is set in its env, as in the Bitbucket and Jira entries, which is Node's default of refusing an unverified certificate: for an instance behind an internal CA add NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS with that CA's .pem. A token can instead be kept out of this entry entirely by running npx @atlassian-dc-mcp/confluence setup once, which stores it in the macOS Keychain.

items.name: Bitbucket
items.description: Bitbucket Server / Data Center pull requests as a reviewer works them: raw unified diffs scoped to a path or glob, inline comments with applyable suggestions, resolve/reopen, approve or request changes, plus grep and blame on any branch for the surrounding code. Runs the MIT package @nexus2520/bitbucket-mcp-server (github.com/pdogra1299/bitbucket-mcp-server) with npx, talks only to the given Bitbucket URL, needs a personal access token from Profile > Personal access tokens there (Bitbucket Cloud wants an app password instead), and its 25 tools arrive on demand. In its entry delete_branch and merge_pull_request refuse main, master and release/*, and NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=1 keeps certificate verification on — for an instance behind an internal CA add NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS with that CA's .pem instead of turning verification off. Needs Node 22+. Cloud: drop BITBUCKET_BASE_URL and give the app password as the token.

items.name: Jira
items.description: Small Jira Server / Data Center server: 13 tools over REST v2 with a personal access token, the one Jira hands out at Profile > Personal Access Tokens (Jira 8.14+) — the issue and its comments, JQL search, workflow transitions, create/update, and attachments kept inside folders you allow. Runs the MIT package @cup0ra/jira-mcp (github.com/cup0ra/jira-mcp) with npx; it talks only to JIRA_BASE_URL, refuses redirects and paths with .., retries reads twice on 429/502/503/504 honouring Retry-After, and never retries a write. Needs Node 20+. It has no TLS or proxy settings of its own: NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=1 keeps certificate verification on — for an instance behind an internal CA add NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS with that CA's .pem instead of turning verification off — and it does not read HTTPS_PROXY. Give the canonical URL including the context path, e.g. https://jira.company.com/jira.

items.name: Kibana, lines around a hit
items.description: Kibana or Elasticsearch logs with the lines around a hit: 3 tools — search by query string within a time range, list indices or index patterns, and get_log_context, which returns the neighbouring entries of a found document. That last one is what makes an error traceable without re-running half a dozen searches. A single Rust binary with no runtime to install: take kibana-mcp-server from github.com/nizovtsevnv/kibana-mcp-server/releases (v0.2.0, a .sha256 sits beside the archive) and put it on PATH, or build it with cargo. It works out for itself whether KIBANA_URL points at Kibana or at Elasticsearch, formats entries by Elastic Common Schema, and speaks stdio. Read-only. For an instance with a self-signed certificate set KIBANA_INSECURE=true, and an API key in KIBANA_API_KEY works instead of the username and password. Treat it as a small, quiet project: one author, last release March 2026.

items.name: Kibana, exact index
items.description: Read Kibana logs without letting the model guess index names: 5 tools — discover the configured sources, describe_fields to find exact-match fields, query over an absolute time window (hits, count, histogram, terms, stats, grouped_top_hits), filter by a known exact field, and configure_index to validate and save the exact index or pattern you name. Runs the MIT package @havesomecode/kibana-mcp-server with npx, read-only, Node 22+, and asks for four values: the Kibana base URL, a login, its password, and the source catalog — the JSON file naming the indexes it may read. The last one is already set to .kibo/kibana-sources.json — relative to the folder open in the app, where the server is started, so the same value works on any machine and needs no home directory in it; put the file there in each project you want this in. An absolute path works too, but a leading ~ does not — neither the app nor the server expands it. A filled-in catalog ships beside this entry as mcp/kibana-exact.sources.example.json: curl it into that .kibo folder and the server starts. Without such a file it refuses to start, which is also why it never scans or auto-selects indexes; the template keeps the default window in the source's description, since start_time and end_time are required arguments. A second Kibana is a second entry with its own catalog and credentials, not a second URL in this one. Instead of all this, running npx -y @havesomecode/kibana-mcp-server bootstrap --client none once saves the connection in the macOS Keychain and the entry needs no env at all.

items.name: Allure TestOps
items.description: Allure TestOps for an agent: 30 named tools for the test-case domain — find cases by name or by AQL, read a case and its steps separately, ask in which launches a case ran, run a selection in a new launch, record a result, read launch statistics, create and update cases and test plans, close and reopen a launch. Runs the MIT server @gribanoveu/mcp-testops (github.com/gribanoveu/mcp-testops) with npx: the package downloads the standalone binary of your platform from its GitHub release once (22–40 MB) into ~/.cache/mcp-testops/ and reuses it, so no Python is needed. It talks only to TESTOPS_BASE_URL, retries reads twice on 429 and 5xx and never retries a write, and answers errors as data ({"ok": false, "error": ...}) instead of failing the call. There is no generic "any path under /api" tool by design, and the HTML duplicates of text fields never leave the server. A deleted case is soft-deleted and cannot be restored through it. Configuration is the entry's own env block, and the server reads seven variables with these defaults: TESTOPS_TOKEN (required — without it the server exits with "TESTOPS_TOKEN is not set"), TESTOPS_BASE_URL https://testops.net, TESTOPS_PROJECT_ID none (then the tools ask for project_id), TESTOPS_TIMEOUT 60 seconds, TESTOPS_VERIFY_SSL false — off by default for a stand on a self-signed CA, turn it on where the certificate is valid, TESTOPS_READ_ONLY false (true registers the 17 read tools only and hides the 13 write ones), MCP_SERVER_NAME testops. Both flags take 1, true, yes or on in any case. Page size (50, at most 100), retries (reads only, 3 attempts on 429/500/502/503/504, writes never) and the log format are not environment settings. The token goes as Authorization: Api-Token <token>, the scheme the stand is expected to take; if it answers 401 or 403, try Bearer. Needs Node 18+; the same release carries a Python wheel, and uvx --from git+https://github.com/gribanoveu/mcp-testops mcp-testops runs it from source.

items.name: Block force push
items.description: Stops the agent's runCommand from running git push --force or -f; --force-with-lease still goes through.

items.name: Block destructive git
items.description: Stops the agent's runCommand from throwing work away with no way back: git reset --hard, git clean -f, git checkout or git restore over the whole tree, git stash drop or clear, git branch -D. One grep over the command line, no network, no files touched, 5 s budget; a command that merely mentions one of these in quotes is stopped too.

items.name: No git add -A
items.description: Stops the agent's runCommand from staging the whole tree with git add -A, git add --all or git add ., so only the files a change is about go in. One grep over the command line, no network, no files touched, 5 s budget.

items.name: Kube delete guard
items.description: Kubernetes role: stops kubeDelete of a StatefulSet or a PersistentVolumeClaim, whose data the app's backup does not carry, and kubeScale to 0, which stops a workload on the agent's own initiative. The namespace is already pinned by the app and cluster-wide kinds are refused, so this guards what the approval card does not. Reads the call's own arguments from stdin, 5 s budget.

items.name: Allure TestOps CLI
items.description: The same Allure TestOps domain, driven from the shell instead of an MCP server: every tool is one command - `npx -y @gribanoveu/mcp-testops call <tool> '<json>'`, with `--list` and `--schema` to look before calling - so the 30 tool descriptions (29 kB) stay out of the context. Carries what the tool cannot say itself: where a token already exists on the machine, that it is never printed or committed, how to pass it for a single command, and how to read each failure once the settings are in place. Includes aql.md with every field, operator and ready-made query. Pick this one when the MCP server is not installed or the context is tight; pick testops-mcp when the server is registered.
